  3HE cB $The |b spectrum end point energy differs from the {+3}H-{+3}He mass   
  3HE2cB difference due to the recoil energy, the final state of the residual   
  3HE3cB system and the mass of the emitted but not detected anti-electron      
  3HE4cB neutrino. In the table above, most of the references that measured the 
  3HE5cB end point energy (EPE) also put upper limits on the neutrino mass.  An 
  3HE6cB early history of the role that the |b decay of {+3}H has played in     
  3HE7cB attempts to measure the neutrino mass can be found in (1988Ro21). Fig. 
  3HE8cB 1 in this article is a graph of the {+3}H |b spectrum near the EPE for 
  3HE9cB the electron neutrino masses of 0 and 30 eV. Fig. 1 in (2006We03) and  
  3HEacB Fig. 3 in (2013Dr11) show the |b spectrum near the end point energy    
  3HEbcB for electron neutrino masses of 0 and 1 eV. Modern refinements of these
  3HEccB measurements have resulted in the upper limit of the electron neutrino 
  3HEdcB mass being just over 2 eV; see (2005Kr03,2010Ot02,2011As10,2013Dr11).

 14B  c  1986Cu01: A beam of {+14}Be ions was produced by fragmenting a         
 14B 2c  540 MeV {+18}O beam on Be and Ta targets. The secondary fragments

 14B 5c  measured in the telescope the rf was scrambled until a decay           
 14B 6c  was measured in the telescope. Analysis of the implantation to         
 14B 7c  decay period, gated on nuclear species, provided the lifetime          
 14B 8c  measurement. T{-1/2}=4.2 ms {I7} was measured.                         
 14B  c  1988Du09: {+14}Be was produced by fragmentation of a 60 MeV/n {+22}Ne  
 14B 2c  beam impinging on either a tantalum or a carbon target and was selected
 14B 3c  using the LISE spectrometer. The |b-particles were                     
 14B 4c  detected by a plastic scintillator while the delayed neutrons          
 14B 5c  were detected through the Gd(n,|g) reaction. T{-1/2}=4.35 ms           
 14B 6c  {I17}, P{-0n}=0.14 {I3}, P{-1n}=0.81 {I4} and P{-2n}=0.05 {I2} were

 14B  c  1995Be25: {+14}Be ions were produced by fragmenting an 80 MeV/A        
 14B 2c  {+18}O beam on a Be target and filtering in the A1200 separator. The   
 14B 3c  beam was implanted in a thick BC412 scintillator during a 10.3 ms      
 14B 4c  accumulation period, followed by either a 10.3 ms or 40 ms beam-off    
 14B 5c  counting period. Beta particles from the decay were detected by        
 14B 6c  the implantation detector, while delayed neutrons were detected        
 14B 7c  using an array of 15 curved scintillator bars that were placed 1 meter 
 14B 8c  from the implantation detector. Neutron energies were deduced from the 
 14B 9c  time-of-flight (tof) between the |b-detector and the neutron array.    
 14B ac  In addition a HPGe detector was placed 83 mm from the implantation     
 14B bc  target.                                                                
 14B  c  Analysis of the data indicated 3-4% contamination from {+11}Li, a      
 14B 2c  correction was possible since the {+11}Li decay had been studied in    
 14B 3c  the same configuration. A neutron detector threshold of                
 14B 4c  0.77 MeV was unfortunately used in the measurements, which led to a    
 14B 5c  significantly low number of |b-n events. The data showed evdence for   
 14B 6c  delayed neutron groups at E{-n}= 3.02 MeV {I3} and 3.52 MeV {I7} with  
 14B 7c  intensities of 0.11% {I2}(stat) {I4}(sys) and 0.30% {I3}(stat)         
 14B 8c  {I5}(sys); the peaks from these weak branches lay ontop of a broad     
 14B 9c  peak that is likely associated with 2n and 3n decay. The multi-neutron 
 14B ac  branching ratio associated with the broad peak is 5% {I1}(stat)        
 14B bc  {I2}(sys). Furthermore, it is plausible that, for example, the         
 14B cc  E{-n}=3.52 MeV neutron group may correspond to sequantial 2n decay.    
 14B  c  Data from the HPGe detector indicated small participation from two     
 14B 2c  known transitions in {+13}B with E{-|g}=3528 keV {I1} and 3680 keV     
 14B 3c  {I1}, however low statistics prevented analysis of the neutron groups  
 14B 4c  that feed these transitions. No 740 keV |g-ray was observed for        
 14B 5c  the transition between the first excited state and ground state.       
 14B  c  A critical issue in the data collection is the relatively low rate of  
 14B 2c  delayed neutron emission. While more than 85% of the decays were       
 14B 3c  expected to be accompanied with neutrons, only about 7% of that        
 14B 4c  intensity is presently observed. It is then suggested that a state     
 14B 5c  in {+14}B, neutron unbound by < 800 keV, is strongly populated.

 14B 7c  significantly complicated the determinations; 4.8 ms {I2}(stat)

 14B 9c  deduced from the |b-n coincidence data.

 14C  c  Activities from numerous reaction products were detected in the        
 14C 2c  target, however by applying a beta particle energy threshold cut to    
 14C 3c  the beta-gamma coincidence data it was possible to select {+14}C       
 14C 4c  gamma-rays that followed the decay of {+14}B.                          
 14C  c  The |b-decay is primarily to {+14}C*(6.09) [J|p=1-] and (6.73) [J|p=3-]

 14C  c  The experimental results are gamma-ray intensities. The measured |g-ray
 14C 2c  intensity ratios are                                                   
 14C 3c  {II}{-6.09}/{II}{-6.73}/{II}{-7.34}=100/(10.0+-2.0)/< 2.2; using these 
 14C 4c  observed intensities and the level decay branching ratios from         
 14C 5c  1970Aj01, the relative beta feedings to the {+14}C*(6.09,6.73,7.34)    
 14C 6c  states was deduced.                                                    
 14C  c  In order to place the relative intensities on an absolute scale the    
 14C 2c  authors estimated the unobserved feeding to the ground state as        
 14C 3c  (5 {I3})%, and they made a further assumption that the %beta-n=0.      
 14C 4c  With these assumptions, which account for (5 {I3})% of the decay, the  
 14C 5c  beta decay branching ratios were deduced by combining the              
 14C 6c  measured |g-ray intensity ratios with the know level gamma-ray decay   
 14C 7c  branching ratios. The absolute beta-branching ratios                   
 14C 8c  I|b{-6.09}/I|b{-6.73}/I|b{-7.34}=(81 {I9})%/(8.6 {I+17-40})%/< 11% were

 14C ac  relative values, however subsequent experiments have produced measured 
 14C bc  values for the beta feeding to the ground state and to neutron unbound

 17C  c  1991Re02,1995ReZZ,2008ReZZ:                                            
 17C 2c  Spallation products from 800 MeV proton bombardment of a               
 17C 3c  {+232}Th target were captured by a transport line with a mass-to-charge
 17C 4c  filter and transferred to the TOFI spectrometer at LAMPF. The          
 17C 5c  beamline was separately tuned to transport a number of different       
 17C 6c  nuclides. The neutrons were detected in a polyethylene moderate {+3}He

 17C 8c  neutron probabilities were deduced from analysis of the number of

 17C bc  the |b-delayed neutron probability                                     
 17C cc  P{-n}(=P{-1n}+2P{-2n}+3P{-3n}+...)=(65 {I35})%

 17C  c  1996Ra02: A beam of {+17}B ions was produced by fragmenting a {+22}Ne  
 17C 2c  beam on a {+9}Be target. The beam was magnetically separated, degraded 
 17C 3c  to lower energies, and finally stopped in a plastic scintillator.      
 17C 4c  The implantation detector was sandwiched between four other            
 17C 5c  scintillator |b-ray detectors.                                         
 17C 6c  A valid {+17}|b decay event required a coincidence between three       
 17C 7c  ajacent detectors. Three neutron walls surrounded the implantation     
 17C 8c  target and covered about 1.4 sr. The decay neutron energy was          
 17C 9c  deduced by the time of flight between the implantation detector and    
 17C Ac  the neutron wall detectors.                                            
 17C  c  The measured neutron spectrum shows two prominent decay groups         
 17C 2c  of {+17}B |b delayed neutrons at E{-n}=2.91 and 1.80 MeV, as           
 17C 3c  well as a strong peak at E{-n}=0.82 MeV from the {+16}N daughter decay.
 17C 4c  A full analysis of the neutron energy spectrum revealed two neutron    
 17C 5c  groups corresponding to known branches in {+16}N decay and four groups 
 17C 6c  at E{-n}=0.42, 1.43, 1.80 and 2.91 MeV that are attributed to          
 17C 7c  neutron decay from {+17}C to {+16}C{-g.s.}.                            
 17C 8c  In later works, the E{-n}=1.43 MeV branch is attributed to decay to    
 17C 9c  {+16}C*(1766) while the E{-n}=0.42 MeV branch is not found.

 17C Bc  normalizing to %|b{+-}{+1}n=(63 {I1})% from (1988Du09).                
 17C  c  2013Ue01,1997YaZX:                                                     
 17C 2c  An E({+22}Ne)=110 MeV/nucleon beam was fragmented in a 1.07 g/cm{+2}

 17C 5c  then implanted at the center of a stack of four 100 |mm thick Pt

 17C 7c  technique was implemented to maximize the sensitivity to spin          
 17C 8c  dependent observables.                                                 
 17C  c  Two plastic scintillators were placed in positions above and below the 
 17C 2c  Pt foil stack and were used to detect |b-rays from decays in the foil. 
 17C 3c  Coincidences among the two foils were used to reject events, for       
 17C 4c  example, from cosmic-ray events.                                       
 17C  c  Neutron bound and neutron unbound states in {+17}C could be populated  
 17C 2c  in the decay, and furthermore the neutron-unbound levels can decay with
 17C 3c  low-energy or high-energy neutron emission.                            
 17C 4c  A 12 element plastic scintillator high-energy neutron detector array   
 17C 5c  (E{-n}|?0.5-10 MeV) covered |W{-n}=0.21|*4|p sr with a 5.6%            
 17C 6c  efficiency for detecting 1 MeV neutrons. The neutron energies          
 17C 7c  were determined by time-of-flight where the |b-ray signal provided a   
 17C 8c  start signal and the neutron array provided the stop signal

 17C cc  0.5 m flight path.

 17C 2c  |g-rays. Plastic scintillator detectors covered the front faces of the

 17C bc  E|b|>10 MeV |b-ray; only peaks corresponding to E|g=217 and 331 keV    
 17C cc  were found.

 17O   H TYP=FUL$AUT=C.G. Sheu,J.H. Kelley,J. Purcell$CUT=5-Aug-2021$CIT=ENSDF$ 
 17O  c  Foreword:                                                              
 17O  c  The measurements of |b-delayed neutrons from {+17}N                    
 17O 2c  decay are relatively consistent in both the energies and relative      
 17O 3c  intensities of neutron groups. Most efforts did not determine the      
 17O 4c  absolute feeding intensities to neutron groups, but rather the         
 17O 5c  relative intensities of neutron groups are reported. The determination 
 17O 6c  of "absolute" intensities relies on a renormalization using an         
 17O 7c  assumption of %|b-n=100-(4.66 {I75}))=(95.34 {I75})%, where            
 17O 8c  4.66 {I75} is the feeding to neutron-bound states (1964Si06).          
 17O  c  1964Si06: {+17}N activity was produced in thin-walled cells comprised  
 17O 2c  of either aluminium or stainless steel using the {+15}N(t,p)           
 17O 3c  reaction. A NaI detector observed the |g-ray spectrum obtained         
 17O 4c  in measurements on the stainless steel cell; transitions at E{-|g}=    
 17O 5c  870 and 2190 keV were observed with a relative ratio=(6.8 {I9}):1.0.   
 17O 6c  Since the 2190 transition corresponds to a cascade from {+17}O*(3055)  
 17O 7c  to {+17}O*(870), the relative feeding of the first and second excited  
 17O 8c  states is (5.8 {I9}):1.0 . Care was taken to minimize contributions    
 17O 9c  from n+p capture that could interfere with the E{-|g}=2190 keV         
 17O ac  analysis. No other |g-rays were observed; in particular transitions    
 17O bc  from {+17}O*(3843:J{+|p}=5/2-) and transitions in {+16}O were not      
 17O cc  observed.                                                              
 17O  c  The measurements on the aluminium cell were analyzed to obtain the     
 17O 2c  singles |b-ray spectrum and the |b-ray plus |g-ray coincidence         
 17O 3c  spectrum. The part of the singles spectrum that extended above the     
 17O 4c  coincidence spectrum was analyzed to obtain the ratio of feeding to    
 17O 5c  {+17}O*(870) relative to feeding to the {+17}O{-g.s.}=(1.7 {I4}):1.0.  
 17O  c  Lastly, the beta spectrum was analyzed to determine the feeding |b-ray 
 17O 2c  intensity to {+17}O*(0,870,3055) relative to the total |b-ray          
 17O 3c  intensity. These decay branches correspond to (4.66 {I75})% of all     
 17O 4c  decays.                                                                
 17O  c  Hence the calculated branching fractions are                           
 17O 2c  (1.55 {I47})% to {+17}O{-g.s.},                                        
 17O 3c  (2.64 {I47})% to {+17}O*(870),                                         
 17O 4c  (0.460 {I11})% to {+17}O*(3055).                                       
 17O 5c  Furthermore, the lack of feeding to {+17}O*(3843:J{+|p}=5/2-) is       
 17O 6c  evidence for assigning J{+|p}=1/2- to {+17}N{-g.s.}.                   
 17O  c  1973De32: {+17}N ions were produced by bombarding 88% enriched {+14}C  
 17O 2c  target which was on a thick tungsten backing with 27-MeV |a-particles. 
 17O 3c  The neutrons were detected with a {+3}He filled proportional counter.  
 17O 4c  Three neutron groups at E{-n}=390 {I16}, 1190 {I30} and 1710 {I40} keV 
 17O 5c  emitted from {+17}O*(4.55,5.09,5.94 MeV) to {+16}O{-g.s.} with         
 17O 6c  branching ratios of 27% {I3}, 57% {I4} and 11% {I2}, respectively.     
 17O 7c  Relative neutron branching ratios are measured, which are normalized   
 17O 8c  to the accepted %|b-n rate of 95%. From the neutron counts in the      
 17O 9c  1.9-2.6 MeV region an upper limit, <0.4%, is set for the branches      
 17O ac  emitted from {+17}O*(6.1-6.8 MeV) to {+16}O{-g.s.}.                    
 17O  c  1973Po11: {+17}N |b{+-}-decay activity was produced by bombarding      
 17O 2c  enriched {+15}N{-2} gas (95-99% {+15}N) using a 2.9-MeV triton beam.   
 17O 3c  The beam was chopped and had 4 second activation and counting periods. 
 17O 4c  The |b activity was detected by a NE102 detector, the |g-decay         
 17O 5c  activity was detected via a 15.2 cm by 12.7 cm NaI detector. The       
 17O 6c  neutron activity was initially measured using a NE102 disk, though     
 17O 7c  issues with high backgrounds at low-energies led to additional         
 17O 8c  measurements using a {+3}He proportional counter. The |b-n and |b-|g   
 17O 9c  coincidences were measured; there is no mention of n-|g coincidences,  
 17O ac  therefore neutron decays are assumed to populate {+16}O{-g.s.}.        
 17O  c  Neutron peaks at 385 {I4}, 1163 {I14} and 1675 {I24} keV were observed 
 17O 2c  corresponding to decays from {+17}O*(4.55,5.38,5.94 MeV) to            
 17O 3c  {+16}O{-g.s.}, respectively. The relative ratios for decay branches    
 17O 4c  were determined, and then the absolute branching ratios were           
 17O 5c  determined by a self-consistent renormalization. The feeding to the    
 17O 6c  {+17}O{-g.s.} relative to {+17}O*(870) was taken from (1964Si06)       
 17O 7c  (=(1.7 {I4}):1.0); other ratios, relative to the E{-n}=1.16 MeV group  
 17O 8c  intensity, were determined. The absolute branching ratios were         
 17O 9c  determined as Branching=(1.7 {I5})% to {+17}O{-g.s.}, (2.9 {I5})% to   
 17O ac  {+17}O*(870), (0.54 {I8})% to {+17}O*(3060), (37.9% {I18}) to          
 17O bc  {+17}O*(4550), (51.1% {I15}) to {+17}O*(5380), and (5.8% {I6}) to      
 17O cc  {+17}O*(5940). The total feeding to bound {+17}O levels was found to   
 17O dc  be (5.14 {I72})%.                                                      
 17O  c  1976Al02: {+17}N ions were produced in the {+15}N(t,p) reaction by     
 17O 2c  bombarding a Ti{+15}N target with 3.0-MeV tritons. The target was      
 17O 3c  irradiated for 4 sec, followed by a 4 sec counting period.             
 17O  c  The |g-ray activity was measured using a Ge(Li) detector. Energies for 
 17O 2c  the {+17}O first and second excited states were determined as 870.8 keV
 17O 3c  {I2} and 3055.2 keV {I3}, and the ratio of the |g ray intensities was  
 17O 4c  measured as 1:(9.6 {I4}). This ratio is significanly different from    
 17O 5c  prior results and is attributed to the ability to resolve the          
 17O 6c  E{-|g}=2190 keV transition from the E{-|g}=2223 keV peak from thermal  
 17O 7c  neutron capture on hydrogen.  No attempt to measure the ground-state   
 17O 8c  branch was made, and hence the values for branching to {+17}O{-g.s.}   
 17O 9c  and {+17}O bound levels was taken from (1964Si06). The branching ratios
 17O ac  were found as (1.6 {I5})% to {+17}O{-g.s.}, (3.0 {I5})% to             
 17O bc  {+17}O*(870), (0.34 {I6})% to {+17}O*(3055).                           
 17O  c  Delayed neutrons were measured using a {+3}He neutron detector; peaks  
 17O 2c  at E{-n}=390, 1160 and 1690 keV were observed. Taking the sum of |b    
 17O 3c  branches to neutron-stable level in {+17}O as (4.9 {I7})%, the         
 17O 4c  branching ratios from {+17}O*(4.55,5.38,5.94 MeV) to {+16}O{-g.s.} are 
 17O 5c  found as 39.2% {I20}, 48.0% {I15} and 7.9% {I7}, respectively.         
 17O  c  1976Oh05: {+17}N |b-decay activity was produced via the                
 17O 2c  {+6}Li(n,|a){+3}H and {+18}O({+3}H,|a){+17}N reactions by              
 17O 3c  placing an enriched {+6}Li{-2}C{+18}O{-3} target (|> 95% {+6}Li, 93.4% 
 17O 4c  {+18}O) in a reactor and utilizing a fast pneumatic tube system to     
 17O 5c  transfer the sample between activation and counting stations. The      
 17O 6c  {+17}N neutron decay curve was measured with eight {+3}He proportional 
 17O 7c  counters surrounded by paraffin. Four peaks at E{-n}=382.8 {I9}, 884   
 17O 8c  {I21} (new identified), 1170.9 {I8} and 1700.3 {I17} keV were measured 
 17O 9c  with |G=54.8 {I4}, 113 {I55}, 63.2 {I11} and 60.5 {I32} keV,           
 17O ac  respectively. Normalization of the neutron emission probabilities to   
 17O bc  P{-n}=95% {I1} from (1964Si06), yields the |b{+-}n branching ratios    
 17O cc  from {+17}O*(4549.3 {I13},5081 {I21}, 5387.1 {12}, 5949.9 {I19} keV)   
 17O dc   to {+16}O{-g.s.} as, 34.8% {I26},                                     
 17O ec  0.6% {I4}, 52.7% {I35} and 7.0% {I5}, respectively.                    
 17O  c  In addition, T{-1/2}=4.174 s {I4} was measured.                        
 17O  c  1984In01: The neutron spectrum of activated cooling water from the     
 17O 2c  SLAC beam dump was analyzed using a {+3}He spectrometer. The activity  
 17O 3c  is presumably from the {+18}O(|g,p){+17}N reaction. In addition to     
 17O 4c  strong neutron lines at E{-n}=383, 1170 and 1700 keV a significantly   
 17O 5c  weaker group at E{-n}=2070 keV is suggested. This group has not been   
 17O 6c  reported in other work.                                                
 17O  c  1991Re02: Spallation products from 800 MeV proton bombardment of a     
 17O 2c  {+232}Th target were captured by a transport line with a mass-to-charge
 17O 3c  filter and transferred to the TOFI spectrometer at LAMPF. The          
 17O 4c  beamline was separately tuned to transport a number of different       
 17O 5c  nuclides. The neutrons were detected in a polyethylene moderate {+3}He 
 17O 6c  counter, and standard techniques were implemented. The |b-delayed      
 17O 7c  neutron probabilities were deduced from analysis of the number of      
 17O 8c  implanted ions (per beam pulse) and the rate of |b-delayed neutrons    
 17O 9c  detected in the zero-threshold counter. The |b-delayed neutron         
 17O ac  probability P{-n}=(102.4 {I60})% was deduced.                          
 17O  c  1996Ra02,2003Mi01: In these experiments, authors observed              
 17O 2c  {+17}N(|b{+-}n) decay to calibrate the neutron energy and the neutron  
 17O 3c  counters. Neutron peaks at 380, 1170 and 1700 keV were observed.       
 17O 4c  The branching ratios of corresponding emissions from                   
 17O 5c  {+17}O*(4.55,5.38,5.94 MeV) to {+16}O{-g.s.} normalized to 95% {I1} are
 17O 6c  39.5% {I46}, 49.1% {I46} and 6.4% {I10}, respectively (1996Ra02).      
 17O 7c  A fourth known peak at E{-n}=880 keV was too weak to be observed.      
 17O  c  2000Bu33,2001Gr06: A {+17}N beam was produced by fragmenting a 77 MeV/A
 17O 2c  {+18}O beam on a Be target; {+17}N was selected by the                 
 17O 3c  LISE3 spectrometer. Neutron time-of-flight (tof) and energy spectra    
 17O 4c  were obtained using the TONNERRE array which covered 45% of 4|p. The   
 17O 5c  intrinsic efficiency is rather high between 1 and 5 MeV. Neutron       
 17O 6c  groups at E{-n}=380, 1170 and 1710 keV were observed. Intensities are  
 17O 7c  not analyzed.                                                          
 17O  c  Comments:                                                              
 17O  c  For the population of bound {+17}O states, the |b-ray energy spectrum  
 17O 2c  analysis of (1964Si06) [Branching({+17}O*(0,870,3055)){-total}=(4.66   
 17O 3c  {I75}) and R=1:(1.7 {I4}) for |b-decay to {+17}O{-g.s.} vs decay to    
 17O 4c  {+17}O*(870)] are combined with R=(9.6 {I4}):1 for the relative        
 17O 5c  intensities of E{-|g}=870 and 2170 keV |g-rays from (1976Al02).        
 17O  c  The data on decay feedings to bound states in {+17}O is sparse;        
 17O 2c  measurements are found in (1964Si06,1973Po11,1976Al02). The only       
 17O 3c  complete measurement on the decay populating {+17}O bound states is    
 17O 4c  found in (1964Si06); along with studying the |g radiations with a NaI  
 17O 5c  detector, they analyzed the |b radiations. In (1964Si06) the ratio of  
 17O 6c  the |b-decay to {+17}O{-g.s.} relative to feeding of {+17}O*(870) is   
 17O 7c  determined as 1:(1.7 {I4}); there is no other comparible measurement.  
 17O 8c  Further analysis of the |b-ray spectrum determined that the bound      
 17O 9c  {+17}O*(0,870,3055) states are populated in (4.66 {I75})% of decays.   
 17O ac  In (1973Po11), use of the (1964Si06) ground state result, along with   
 17O bc  analysis of their NaI data results in finding the branching ratio to   
 17O cc  {+17}O*(0,870,3055) as (5.14 {I72})%, but, as mentioned below, it is   
 17O dc  suggested that the E{-|g}=2170 keV intensity is enlarged by a          
 17O ec  systematic error associated with contributions from n+p capture. In    
 17O fc  (1973Po11) one finds the only reported connection between any neutron  
 17O gc  group intensity and a |g-ray transition intensity:                     
 17O hc  I(|g{-870 keV})/I(E{-n}=1.16 MeV)=(0.0667 {I95}).                      
 17O ic  In (1976Al02) the value R=(9.6 {I4}):1 for the relative                
 17O jc  intensities of E{-|g}=870 and 2170 keV |g-rays is found; they suggest  
 17O kc  the results of (1964Si06,1973Po11) are unreliable because neither      
 17O lc  group could resolve n+p capture |g rays from the 2170 keV decay        
 17O mc  transition; in spite of great caution described in those works this    
 17O nc  uncertainty discounts their E{-|g}=2170 keV intensities.               
 17O  c                                                                         
 17O  c  In all cases, the neutron group branching ratios are based on          
 17O 2c  relative intensity measurements that are normalized to unity with      
 17O 3c  inclusion of feedings to {+17}O bound states.                          
 17O  c  There are discrepancies among the relative intensities reported in     
 17O 2c  (1973De32,1973Po11,1976Al02,1976Oh05,1996Ra02). In the present analysis
 17O 3c  all measurements are considered; the results of (1973De32) appear to   
 17O 4c  deviate significantly from other measurements and are excluded from    
 17O 5c  analysis. The mean intensities from the remaining four measurements are
 17O 6c  determined after normalizing each measurement to the strongest         
 17O 7c  decay transition. These intensities are then renormalized to yield     
 17O 7c  %|b-n=(100-(4.66 {I75}))=(95.34 {I75})%.

 18N     18C B- DECAY                  1991PR03                  ENSDF    202110
 18N   H TYP=FUL$AUT=R. Spitzer, J.H. Kelley$CUT=30-Jun-2021$CIT=ENSDF$         
 18N  c  {IDecay to neutron-bound levels}:                                      
 18N  c  1991Pr03: A beam of {+18}C, produced using the GANIL/LISE facility,    
 18N 2c  was implanted into a plastic scintillator.                             
 18N 3c  Activity was collected for 300 ms followed by                          
 18N 4c  an equal time of decay counting.                                       
 18N 5c  A 40% relative efficience HPGe detector was placed near the stopper,   
 18N 6c  and decay events were recorded for |b and |b-|g coincidence events.    
 18N 7c  The authors aimed to resolve the |b{+-}0n and |b{+-}1n decay branches. 
 18N 8c  In the article, the decay of {+18}C and {+18}N were measured           
 18N 9c  under identical experimental conditions; then the ratio of             
 18N ac  the intensity of the {+18}O E{-|g}=1982 keV transition, which is       
 18N bc  strongly populated in {+18}N decay, was analyzed to determine the      
 18N cc  sum of {+18}C decay branches to bound {+18}N states. %|b{+-}0n=81 {I5} 
 18N dc  was deduced. This implies %|b{+-}1n=19 {I5}.                           
 18N  c  A total of 9 |g-ray {+18}N transitions were identified along           
 18N 2c  with others associated with {+17}N and {+18}O. The |g-ray              
 18N 3c  intensities are presented in two formats: first- they are given as     
 18N 4c  relative intensities normalized to the strongest line (Table 1), the   
 18N 5c  E{-|g}=2614 keV transition; second- intensities are given for a        
 18N 6c  100% branching sum out of each level (Table 3).                        
 18N  c  The authors discussed the likelihood of |g-ray summing effects as a    
 18N 2c  potential source of systematic uncertainty; this is because a single   
 18N 3c  HPGe detector was used and it was placed close to the decay            
 18N 4c  stopper foil. Secondly, they discussed an inconsistency of their data  
 18N 5c  where a higher intensity feeds the E{-x}=115 keV level than is         
 18N 6c  observed exiting the level. Authors suggest this inconsistency may be  
 18N 7c  attributed to the state having a long lifetime causing                 
 18N 8c  a significan fraction (|?1/2) to fall outside the DAQ                  
 18N 9c  coincidence window.                                                    
 18N  c  The evaluator finds significant problems with the                      
 18N 2c  intensity balance for the E{-x}=115 and 572 keV level |g rays;         
 18N 3c  the E{-x}=115 keV level lifetime is about a ns (2008Wi05). For         
 18N 4c  the analysis, the decay intensities are set equal to the feeding       
 18N 5c  intensities for these two states. Furthermore there is a discrepancy   
 18N 6c  in the decay branching ratios of {+18}N*(1734) state given in          
 18N 7c  Table 1 vs. Table 3. We take the Table 1 values, since they should     
 18N 8c  require less interpretation to obtain, and since they are required     
 18N 9c  to arrive at their deduced relative |b{+-} branching ratios.           
 18N  c  In spite of the experimental uncertainties, (1991Pr03) is the only     
 18N 2c  {+18}C |b{+-} decay study that provides |g-ray spectroscopy information
 18N 3c  on {+18}N levels. In their analysis, the authors suggest a negligible  
 18N 4c  first-forbidden branch to {+18}N{-g.s.}, and so they normalize their   
 18N 5c  measured relative branching ratios with %|b{+-}0n=81 {I5} to obtain    
 18N 6c  the absolute decay intensities.                                        
 18N  c  The following table is from (1991Pr03). It gives the measured energies 
 18N 2c  and relative intensities of |g-rays assigned to the |b{+-} decay of    
 18N 3c  {+18}C. The two entries marked with {+17}N involve beta delayed neutron
 18N 4c  emission.

 18N  c  {IDecay to neutron-unbound levels}:                                    
 18N  c  1991Pr03: As mentioned above, %|b{+-}1n=19 {I5} was deduced            
 18N 2c  by comparing the measured |g-ray yields from {+18}C and                
 18N 3c  {+18}N decay reactions.                                                
 18N  c  1988Mu08,1989Le16: {+18}C ions from fragmentation of {+86}Kr           
 18N 2c  (1988Mu08) and {+48}Ca (1989Le16) on a {+181}Ta target at GANIL        
 18N 3c  were selected using the LISE spectrometer and implanted into a         
 18N 4c  Si detector. The telescope was surrounded by a thin plastic            
 18N 5c  scintillator |b counter and segmented 4|p NE102A scintillator          
 18N 6c  neutron array.                                                         
 18N 7c  Neutron energy thresholds of 440 keV and 350 keV were utilized in      
 18N 8c  (1988Mu08) and (1989Le16), respectively. Delayed neutron emission      
 18N 9c  probabilities of P{-n}=(25.0 {I45})% and (50 {I10})% were deduced,     
 18N ac  respectively.                                                          
 18N  c  1991Re02: {+18}C spallation products from 800 MeV proton bombardment   
 18N 2c  of a {+232}Th target were transported to the TOFI spectrometer at      
 18N 3c  LAMPF. The ions were implanted in a Si detector.                       
 18N 4c  The |b-delayed neutrons were detected in a                             
 18N 5c  polyethylene moderated {+3}He counter; half-lives and |b-delayed       
 18N 6c  neutron probabilities were deduced from analysis of the number of      
 18N 7c  implanted ions (per beam pulse) and the rate of |b-delayed neutrons    
 18N 8c  detected in the zero-threshold counter. The |b-delayed neutron         
 18N 9c  probability =(43.3 {I65})% was deduced along with T{-1/2}=94 ms {I27}. 
 18N  c  New data was collected using the experimental                          
 18N 2c  configuration of (1991Re02), and the collective results were analyzed. 
 18N 3c  In (1994ReZZ) P{-n}=(30.2 {I17})% and T{-1/2}=92.9 ms {I53} are        
 18N 4c  given. In later unpublished works (1995ReZZ,2008ReZZ),                 
 18N 5c  P{-n}=(31.5 {I15})% and T{-1/2}=92 ms {I5} are indicated.              
 18N 6c  Other analyses of these data are found in (1993ReZX,1994KiZU).         
 18N  c  1995Sc03: A {+18}C beam from the NSCL/A1200 was stopped in a           
 18N 2c  plastic scintillator implantaion detector that was surrounded by an    
 18N 3c  array of 15 plastic scintillator neutron detectors. The beam was       
 18N 4c  collected in the stopping detector for 206 ms followed by a 222 ms     
 18N 5c  beam-off counting period. Neutron events are recorded for |b signals   
 18N 6c  in the implantation detector in coincidence with neutron signals in the
 18N 7c  99.7 cm flight path neutron array. Neutron energies were determined    
 18N 8c  via time-of-flight; the array was configured with a low-energy         
 18N 9c  threshold of |?750 keV. Background activity from {+18}N and {+17}N,    
 18N ac  the {+18}C decay daughters, was separable from the {+18}C decays.      
 18N  c  Seven neutron groups are evident in the energy spectrum; however,      
 18N 2c  the lack of n-|g coincidence data and unknown spectroscopy             
 18N 3c  of {+18}N levels above the neutron binding precludes assignment of     
 18N 4c  the neutron groups to {+18}N levels. This is further accented by the   
 18N 5c  known participation of {+17}N*(1374,1850) levels in the |b{+-}n        
 18N 6c  reaction as reported in (1991Pr03). The intensity of |b{+-}n neutron   
 18N 7c  events reported in (1995Sc03) is (21.4 {I44})%. The neutrons can       
 18N 8c  go to {+17}N*(0,1374,1849), which implies {+18}N excitation energies   
 18N 9c  listed below.

 18N  c  {IComments}:                                                           
 18N  c  The P{-n}=(31.5 {I15})%=%|b{+-}1n value from (2008ReZZ) is             
 18N 2c  reluctantly accepted. The evaluator notes that amongst the Kim/Reeder  
 18N 3c  articles and conference reports, a wide range of values are presented. 
 18N 4c  Measurements listed above using neutron arrays having finite           
 18N 5c  neutron-energy thresholds found discrete neutron groups adding to      
 18N 6c  |?20% of the decay intensities; however, because the                   
 18N 7c  moderated {+3}He counter used by Reeder                                
 18N 8c  is sensitive to all energy neutrons, this approach should              
 18N 9c  provide the most reliable P{-n} value.                                 
 18N  c  Taking %|b{+-}1n=(31.5 {I15}), the relative intensities of             
 18N 2c  |g transitions reported in (1991Pr03) are normalized to                
 18N 3c  give %|b{+-}0n=(68.5 {I15}). In (1991Pr03), the feeding into           
 18N 4c  {+18}N*(115,572) states is greater than the decay out of the states,   
 18N 5c  which required adjustments to the intensity balance.                   
 18N  c  See theoretical discussion on |b decay in (1993Ch06); also see         
 18N 2c  (2016Ta07).

 19C  c  1998Yo06: A beam of {+19}B was produced by fragmentation of a 95 MeV/A 
 19C 2c  {+40}Ar beam on a {+181}Ta target. {+19}B was selected using the RIKEN 
 19C 3c  Projectile-fragment Separator (RIPS) and was implanted into a 12 mm    
 19C 4c  thick plastic scintillator stopper. The |b-decays were observed during 
 19C 5c  the 100 ms beam-off period. The active stopper detected |b-rays and a  
 19C 6c  neutron detector array, consisting of 14 liquid scintillation counters 
 19C 7c  covering about 80% of 4|p detected delayed neutrons. The efficiency of 
 19C 8c  the neutron array was 30% by comparison of a measurement of |b-delayed 
 19C 9c  neutrons of {+15}B, which has a known delayed neutron emission         
 19C ac  probability of 100%.                                                   
 19C  c  A preliminary value of T{-1/2}=3.3 ms {I2} was deduced from the        
 19C 2c  least-squares fits to the data, and P{-n}=125% {I32} was determined    
 19C 3c  from the ratio of the number of detected neutrons to that of |b-rays.  
 19C 4c  P{-n} is more than 100% which implies the existence of significant     
 19C 5c  multineutron emissions in the decay, reflecting its large Q{-|b} value 
 19C 6c  (26.5 MeV) compared with the multineutron separation energies of       
 19C 7c  daughter nucleus {+19}C (S{-1n}=160 keV, S{-2n}=4.4 MeV,.....).        
 19C  c  2003Yo02: The authors reevaluated the preliminary values T{-1/2} and   
 19C 2c  P{-n} reported in 1998Yo06. The new experiment was performed using     
 19C 3c  RIPS at RIKEN Accelerator Research Facility as was in 1998Yo06. A beam 
 19C 4c  of {+19}B was produced by the projectile-fragmentation reaction of a   
 19C 5c  95 MeV/{Iu} {+40}Ar beam on a 670 mg/cm{+2} {+nat}Ta target. The values
 19C 6c  of T{-1/2} and P{-{Ii}n} were determined by fitting a set of decay     
 19C 7c  curves altogether to remove possible complication and inconsistency.   
 19C 8c  The method of maximum likelihood was applied for deducing T{-1/2} and  
 19C 9c  P{-{Ii}n}. The neutron detection efficiencies were treated carefully,  
 19C ac  the total detection efficiencies of direct and scattered neutrons are  
 19C bc  31.5 % {I3} and 4.7% {I+2}{I-6}, respectively. The new values of       
 19C cc  T{-1/2}=2.92 ms {I13}, P{-1n}=71.8% {I+83}{I-91} and P{-2n}=16.0%      
 19C dc  {I+56}{I-48} were determined with a better precision. P{-3n} was not   
 19C ec  determined because of the limited statistics. In the text it is unclear
 19C fc  if the 1998Yo06 "preliminary" data are included in the 2003Yo02        
 19C gc  analysis; we assume that it is and use the 2003Yo02 result to avoid    
 19C hc  possible data correlations.                                            
 19C  c  1999Re16: A low statistics determination of T{-1/2}=4.5 ms {I15} was   
 19C 2c  given.                                                                 
 19C  c  In Summary, the decay to {+19}C levels is not measured. Only the       
 19C 2c  P{-1n}=71.8% {I+83}{I-91} to {+18}C and P{-2n}=16.0%                   
 19C 3c  {I+56}{I-48} to {+17}C were determined.

 19N  c  1995Oz02: A beam of {+19}C ions, produced by fragmenting a {+22}Ne     
 19N 2c  beam on a {+9}Be target, was magnetically separated and degraded       
 19N 3c  to lower energies before being stopped in a plastic scintillator. The  
 19N 4c  implantation detector was sandwiched between four other scintillator   
 19N 5c  detectors; a valid event required a coincidence between three          
 19N 6c  ajacent detectors. Three neutron walls surrounded the implantation     
 19N 7c  target and covered about 1.4 sr. The decay neutron energy was deduced  
 19N 8c  by the time of flight between the implantation detector and the        
 19N 9c  neutron wall detectors. The time-of-flight (tof) was calibrated by     
 19N ac  studying the decay of {+17}N which has three visible known neutron     
 19N bc  groups. A set of two NaI detectors faced the target for use            
 19N cc  measuring |g-ray singles events and n-|g coincidence events.           
 19N  c  The measured neutron spectrum shows several decay groups. A significant
 19N 2c  {+17}B component was present in the beam, and its decay radiations     
 19N 3c  presented a background that was analyzed and subtracted. The final     
 19N 4c  analysis of the neutron energy spectrum revealed five neutron groups   
 19N 5c  that are attributed to |b delayed neutron decay of {+19}C, or its      
 19N 6c  daughter {+19}N.                                                       
 19N  c  Throughout the experiment, ions were implanted for a 100 ms period     
 19N 2c  followed by a 200 ms counting period; analysis of the time dependence  
 19N 3c  for the neutron groups permitted assignment of four groups to decay of 
 19N 4c  {+19}C (T{-1/2}|?50 ms) and one group to decay of {+19}N (T{-1/2}|?320 
 19N 5c  ms).                                                                   
 19N  c  Four neutron groups at E{-n}=0.46, 1.01, 1.50 and 2.08 keV are         
 19N 2c  observed; poor statistics prohibited full analysis of the E{-n}=2.08   
 19N 3c  MeV group. Three excited states of {+19}N were deduced from these E{-n}
 19N 4c  energies. The results are presented                                    
 19N 5c  by normalizing to %|b{+-}1n=47% {I3} from

 19O  c  2006Su12: {+19}N ions from fragmentation of an 80 MeV/u {+22}Ne beam   
 19O 2c  on a Be target were selected by the NSCL A1200 fragment separator and

 19O 9c  revealed eight neutron groups to {+18}O states. |g transitions among   
 19O ac  excited states in {+19}O and {+18}O were also observed. A detailed     
 19O bc  decay scheme is suggested by comparison of the |g transition           
 19O cc  intensities amongst the {+19}O levels, |b-|g-n coincidences, and a     
 19O dc  reasonable placement of neutron group intensties that could give an    
 19O ec  intensity balance. Neutron emission groups with intensities less than  
 19O fc  1% are left unplaced in the decay scheme. T{-1/2}=336 ms {I3} was also 
 19O xc  measured.

 30MG c  2020Ni05: The {+30}Na nuclear-spin-polarized beam, E=28 MeV, was       
 30MG2c  produced by fragmentation of uranium carbide (UC{-x}) traget with 500  
 30MG3c  MeV protons at the ISAC facility of TRIUMF following collinear optical 
 30MG4c  pumping at the polarizer and was delivered and stopped in vacuum on a  
 30MG5c  20-|mm-thick Pt foil at the experimental setup for the |b-|g           
 30MG6c  spectroscopy. The polarization of {+30}Na was 31% {I1}. Eight sets of  
 30MG7c  detector telescopes consisting of a coaxial HPGe and thin plastic      
 30MG8c  scintillators(s). Six other telescopes were placed in a plane          
 30MG9c  perpendicular to the polarization direction. Measured E|g, I|g, spatial
 30MGac  asymmetry of |b in coin with |g rays. Deduced level scheme, spin,      
 30MGbc  parity.                                                                
 30MG c  1989Ba07: {+30}Na was produced bombarding a uranium carbide target with
 30MG2c  600 MeV protons from the CERN synchrocyclotron, mass separated in the  
 30MG3c  ISOLDE facility; NE213 scintillator, 2 HPGe detectors and one          
 30MG4c  neutron detector; Measured: E|g, I|g, |g|g coin, |g-n coin.            
 30MG c  1984Gu19: {+30}Na was produced in the fragmentation of iridium target  
 30MG2c  by 10 GeV protons from the CERN synchrotron, recoiled fragments were   
 30MG3c  thermalized, ionized and mass-separated; Ge(Li) detector; measured     
 30MG4c  E|g, |b-|g|g coin, absolute I|g.                                       
 30MG c  2009Sc11: {+30}Na source was produced by bombarding a UC{-x}/graphite  
 30MG2c  target with 1.4 GeV protons at CERN PS Booster facility; Mass          
 30MG3c  separation of the reaction products was done by the ISOLDE;            
 30MG4c  Measured |b(ce) coin using a liquid nitrogen cooled Si(Li) detector in 
 30MG5c  conjunction with a (mini-orange) magnetic transport system. The |g-rays
 30MG6c  following |b{+-} decay were measured using a Ge detector.

 30MG2c  4 of which are listed in the comments. 336.3, 1041.2, and 1510.7|g are 
 30MG3c  not reported/confirmed in the later works.

 31MG c  2019Ni04,2017Ni02: {+31}Na was produced in the fragmentation of Uranium
 31MG2c  Carbide target with 500-MeV protons at the ISAC-TRIUMF facility. Ions  
 31MG3c  of singly-charged {+31}Na with an energy of 28 keV were separated using
 31MG4c  a high resolution mass separator, and were polarized by simultaneous   
 31MG5c  pumping of both sub-levels of the atomic ground-state by two laser     
 31MG6c  frequencies. At the counting station, static magnetic field of 0.53 T  
 31MG7c  was applied along the polarization direction. Measured E|g, I|g,       
 31MG8c  |g|g-coin, |b|g-coin, level half-life by |b|g(t), and |b polarization  
 31MG9c  asymmetries gated by |g rays using eight detector telescopes. Deduced  
 31MGAc  levels, J, |p, |b feedings, log| {Ift} values. Comparison with         
 31MGBc  antisymmetrized molecular dynamics (AMD) plus generator coordinate     
 31MGCc  method (GCM). Data in 2017Ni02 are superseded by those in 2019Ni04.    
 31MG c  1993Kl02: Na isotopes were produced by bombarding an Uranium Carbide   
 31MG2c  target with 600 MeV protons from the CERN synchrocyclotron and         
 31MG3c  separated by the ISOLDE2 separator. |b particles were detected with    
 31MG4c  a thin plastic scintillator, neutrons were detected with a liquid      
 31MG5c  scintillator, and |g rays were detected with two Ge detectors. Measured
 31MG6c  E|g, I|g, |b|g-coin, |b|g|g-coin, |b|g-n-coin. Deduced levels, J, |p,  
 31MG7c  branching ratios, log {Ift}.                                           
 31MG c  1984Gu19: Na isotopes were produced by bombarding a 30 g/cm{+2} Ir     
 31MG2c  target with 10 GeV proton beam from the CERN synchrotron. Fragments    
 31MG3c  were separated and collected into a thin stainless steel tube. |g rays 
 31MG4c  were detected with two Ge(Li) detectors and |b particles were detected 
 31MG5c  with two plastic scintillators. Measured E|g, I|g, |b|g(t), |b|g-coin, 
 31MG6c  |b|g|g-coin. Deduced levels, T{-1/2}, |g-ray branching ratios,         
 31MG7c  |b-delayed neutron-emission probabilities. Other papers from the same  
 31MG8c  group with the same experimental setup are 1984La03: measured %|b{+-}n,
 31MG9c  half-life and |bn-coin; 1983De04: measured Q value, |b|g-coin.         
 31MG c  1979De02: {+31}Na from U(p,X) E(p)=24 GeV at CERN. Measured E|g, I|g,  
 31MG2c  |g(t), |b|g-coin, |b|g|g-coin. Deduced levels, T{-1/2}. 1980De26 from  
 31MG3c  the same group produced the source also using 600 MeV protons, measured
 31MG4c  E|g, I|g, |bn(t).

 47K  c  2004We09: {+47}Ar activity produced by 1.4 GeV protons from the PSB    
 47K 2c  accelerator impinging on a standard ISOLDE uranium carbide graphite

 47K 4c  {Ivia} a low-temperature, water-cooled transfer line to a standard     
 47K 5c  FEBIAD MK-7 plasma ion source, where the ionization by plasma          
 47K 6c  discharge took place. A tungsten converter to produce neutrons by the  
 47K 7c  proton beam was placed parallel to the target, allowing one to switch  
 47K 8c  to the neutron irradiation of the target by changing the focus of the  
 47K 9c  proton beam from the target to the converter. In comparison to the     
 47K ac  proton reaction, the neutron-induced reaction can suppress extreme     
 47K bc  asymmetric fission products such as {+47}Ar. Thus, the two different

 71NI c  2012Ra10 (also 2005Ma95,2010RaZY)): {+71}Co produced in fragmentation  
 71NI2c  of 140 MeV/nucleon {+86}Kr beam with a {+9}Be target at NSCL-MSU       
 71NI3c  facility, followed by separation of fragments using A1900 fragment     
 71NI4c  separator. The ions were implanted in double-sided silicon strip (DSSD)
 71NI5c  detectors for detection of (fragment)|b correlated events. SeGA        
 71NI6c  |g-detector array containing 16 HPGe detectors was used for E|g, I|g,  
 71NI7c  |g|g- and |b|g-coin and isotopic half-life measurements. Detailed      
 71NI8c  shell-model calculations using NR78 residual interaction               
 71NI d  2008RaZY conference report and 2010RaZY preprint superseded by 2012Ra10
 71NI c  2019Ly02: {+71}Co from {+86}Kr beam at 140 MeV/nucleon impinging on    
 71NI2c  a {+9}Be target at the NSCL-MSU facility. {+71}Co, was identified      
 71NI3c  using energy loss and time-of-flight information from a plastic        
 71NI4c  scintillator detector in the focal plane of the A1900 and two silicon  
 71NI5c  PIN detectors, followed by implantation in a 1-mm thick double-sided   
 71NI6c  silicon strip detector (DSSD) which was placed in the geometric center 
 71NI7c  of the Summing NaI(Tl) (SuN) detector. Measured total absorption       
 71NI8c  |g spectrum (TAGS), |b-decay branching ratios, B(>), parent half       
 71NI9c  life. Comparison with theoretical calculations using different models. 
 71NI c  2012Ra10 mentioned an additional experiment at NSCL (reference 36 in   
 71NI2c  2012Ra10) dealing with on-line spectroscopy for {+71}Ni in a           
 71NI3c  knockout reaction on {+73}Cu beam and probably {+9}Be target, where    
 71NI4c  281-, 567- and 813-keV |g rays were seen, none of these in coincidence 
 71NI5c  mode. This observation confirms the placement of these |g rays in      
 71NI6c  {+71}Co

 71NI5c  to {+71}Ni was taken by 2009St07 from November 2007 Sanibel Island

 76ZN c  2022Si25: {+76}Cu activity from 54-MeV proton beam on a UC{-x} target  
 76ZN2c  at HRIBF at ORNL. Fragments passed through a low-resolution mass       
 76ZN3c  separator to select A=76 nuclei and then a high-resolution mass        
 76ZN4c  separator. {+76}Zn passed into LeRIBSS and implanted into a moving     
 76ZN5c  tape. Measured E|g, I|g, |g|g, |b|g using four HPGe detectors and two  
 76ZN6c  plastic scintillators.                                                 
 76ZN c  2005Va19 (also 2002VaZX thesis): {+76}Cu produced by {+238}U(n,F)      
 76ZN2c  and {+238}U(p,F) at ISOLDE facility, measured E|g, I|g, |g|g, |b|g,    
 76ZN3c  timing of |b|g and |g|g coin spectra                                   
 76ZN c  1990Wi12: measured |g, |g|g, (integral |b)(|g) coin for T{-1/2} of     
 76ZN2c  {+76}Cu decay                                                          
 76ZN c  2021Ch56: {+76}Cu ion beam was produced in {+9}Be({+86}Kr,X) at        
 76ZN2c  E({+86}Kr)=140 MeV/nucleon incident energy, followed by separation of  
 76ZN3c  fragments of interest using A1900 fragment separator at NSCL-MSU       
 76ZN4c  facility. Ions were implanted into a CeBr{-3} scintillator, coupled to 
 76ZN5c  a position-sensitive photomultiplier tube (PSPMT) consisting of a      
 76ZN6c  single dynode and 256 anodes arranged, and identified event-by-event   
 76ZN7c  using the |DE-tof method. Measured (ions)|b-correlations, E|g, I|g,    
 76ZN8c  |b|g- and |g|g-coin, level half-life by |g|g(t) using and array of     
 76ZN9c  15 LaBr{-3} detectors and array of 16 HPGe clover detectors. Main      
 76ZNAc  experimental finding of this work is in the identification of a 25-ns  
 76ZNBc  isomer in {+76}Zn at 2634 keV. Detailed comparison with shell-model    
 76ZNCc  calculations using jj44b, jj44c and JUN45 interactions.

 76ZN d  The decay scheme proposed in 2005Va19 is modified in several ways from 
 76ZN2d  the first one proposed by 1990Wi12. The 1031 and 1716 levels from      
 76ZN3d  1990Wi12 are omitted, 1761 level in 1990Wi12 is replaced by 2349 level,
 76ZN4d  and 2266, 3233 and 3273 levels are newly established by 2005Va19 based 
 76ZN5d  on |g|g-coincidence data. These changes are due to reassignment or     
 76ZN6d  non-observation of certain |g rays reported by 1990Wi12 from the decay 
 76ZN7d  of {+76}Cu. A 1783-431 cascade in 1990Wi12 from a 2813 level was not   
 76ZN8d  confirmed by 2015Va19, both the |g rays were assigned to the decay of  
 76ZN9d  {+76}Ga instead, based on laser on and off set up and their observation
 76ZNad  in coincidence with other |g rays from the decay of {+76}Ga. A 431|g is
 76ZNbd  present in the {+76}Ga decay dataset, originating from a 1539 level in 
 76ZNcd  {+76}Ge, but the 1783|g is absent in this dataset. A 1098-419 cascade  
 76ZNdd  in 1990Wi12, populating a 1716 level was not confirmed by 2005Va19     
 76ZNed  since no 1098|g was seen and 419|g was reassigned to the decay of a new

 77ZN c  2009Il01, 2009Wi03: {+77}Cu isotope produced in the reaction           
 77ZN2c  {+238}U(p,F) with a 50 MeV beam provided by the HRIBF facility at      
 77ZN3c  ORNL, RIB facility. The radioactive beams were extracted and mass      
 77ZN4c  separated. Detected decay products with a Micro-channel plate detector,
 77ZN5c  an ionization chamber and a moving tape collector.                     
 77ZN3c  In one experiment, the Cu ions were accelerated to 225 MeV and

 77ZN c  2009Pa35: {+77}Cu produced in the fission of uranium (target=uranium   
 77ZN2c  carbide) by spallation neutrons which were produced by 1 GeV protons   
 77ZN3c  hitting a tantalum target. The {+77}Cu nuclei were selected by         
 77ZN4c  Resonant Ionization Laser Ion Source (RILIS) and General Purpose       
 77ZN5c  mass separator (GPS) at the CERN-ISOLDE facility. The separated        
 77ZN6c  {+77}Cu nuclei at a typical energy of 60 keV were implanted on a tape  
 77ZN7c  surrounded by three E-|DE plastic detectors for |b-particle detection  
 77ZN8c  and two HPGe detectors. Measured |g, |b, |b|g coin, |b|b coin,         
 77ZN9c  |g|g coin and delayed-neutron events. The neutrons were detected with  
 77ZNAc  the Mainz neutron long counter. Major contribution to |g-ray and       
 77ZNBc  |b spectra are from {+77}Ga decay as indicated by a comparison of      
 77ZNCc  'laser-on' and 'laser-off' spectra. In both the spectra, lines from    
 77ZNDc  {+77}Ga are quite prominent. The decay scheme of {+77}Ga is poorly     
 77ZNEc  known. By subtraction procedures, 2009Pa35 obtained a spectrum         
 77ZNFc  which mainly contained lines from {+77}Cu activity. In the presence    
 77ZNGc  of the impurities, singles |b spectrum could not be obtained, thus     
 77ZNHc  no information could be obtained for |b feeding to the ground state

 86BR c  2016Ur04: {+86}Se produced in the fission of {+235}U induced by        
 86BR2c  thermal neutrons from PF1B-ILL-Grenoble facility, and separated using  
 86BR2c  Lohengrin fission-fragment separator. The cumulative yield for {+86}Se 
 86BR3c  was 1.2%. Measured E|g, I|g, |g|g-coin using an array of Ge            
 86BR4c  detectors at ILL-Grenoble. Deduced levels, J|p, configurations.        
 86BR5c  Comparison with large-scale shell-model calculations                   
 86BR c  1980Ze04 (also 1978ZeZZ): Measured E|g, I|g, |g|g-coin at Mainz reactor
 86BR2c  facility. A total of 21 |g rays from 48.3 keV to 2660.0 keV were       
 86BR3c  reported with relative intensities. Absolute intensities (I|g/100      
 86BR4c  decays) were also deduced with reference to I|g(absolute)=63% for      
 86BR5c  the 1564.7|g from {+86}Br to {+86}Kr decay. Uncertainties for E|g      
 86BR6c  values were stated as 0.3 keV for stronger and 0.5 keV for weaker      
 86BR7c  |g rays. No intensities were given for I|g values.                     
 86BR c  Others:                                                                
 86BR c  1982Li09: measured absolute |g intensity (per 100 decays of {+86}Se)   
 86BR2c  for the 1399|g using a continuous gas-phase rapid chemistry            
 86BR3c  system, with reference to 1565|g from the decay of {+86}Br.            
 86BR c  1977Pf01: eight |g rays reported from 47.6 keV to 2661.0 keV with      
 86BR2c  intensities. Half-life of {+86}Se measured as 14 s {I2} using LOHENGRIN
 86BR3c  mass separator                                                         
 86BR c  1975Hu02: measured half-life of {+86}Se decay as 14.4 s {I10} from     
 86BR2c  average of decay curves for seven |g rays. Seven |g rays reported from 
 86BR3c  788 keV to 2662 keV with I|g values.                                   
 86BR c  1973Ta19: eight |g rays reported from 49 to 1400 keV, with intensities 
 86BR2c  and half-lives of {+86}Se decay. Three half-lives measured were:       
 86BR3c  14.4 s {I20} for 49.0|g, 14.3 s {I5} for 154.3|g and 15.9 s {I12} for  
 86BR4c  207.7|g. Four other half-lives measured were listed without            
 86BR5c  uncertainties. Strong |g rays reported at 941.3 keV (I|g=237);         
 86BR6c  1081.1 keV (I|g=257); 1208.3 keV (I|g=293) and 1340.2 keV (I|g=188)    
 86BR7c  were not confirmed in later studies of this decay.                     
 86BR c  1960Sa05: measured half-life of a 16 s {I3} activity which was         
 86BR2c  assigned by 1960Sa05 due to {+86}Se or {+87}Se. However, known         
 86BR3c  half-life of 5.50 s {I14} for {+87}Se in ENSDF database (July 2015     
 86BR4c  update) favors the assignment of activity to {+86}Se.

 86KR2 H CUT=20-Jan-2025$                                                       
 86KR c  2016Ur04: {+86}Br obtained from the decay of {+86}Se decay, which was  
 86KR2c  produced in the fission of {+235}U induced by thermal neutrons from    
 86KR3c  PF1B-ILL-Grenoble facility, and separated using Lohengrin              
 86KR4c  fission-fragment separator. The cumulative yield for {+86}Se           
 86KR5c  was 1.2%. Measured E|g, I|g, |g|g-coin, |g|g(|q) for 0|', 45|' and     
 86KR6c  90|', |g|g(linear polarization) using an array of Ge detectors at      
 86KR7c  ILL-Grenoble. For |g|g(|q) data, eight EXOGAM Clover detectors         
 86KR8c  of EXILL array were used. Deduced levels, J|p, mixing ratios.          
 86KR9c  Comparison with large-scale shell-model calculations. Communications   
 86KRAc  with W. Urban (first author of 2016Ur04) between May 04-08, 2023 have  
 86KRBc  been considered in this dataset.                                       
 86KR c  2017Ri08: {+87}Br produced in U(p,F) reaction, followed by mass        
 86KR2c  separation using the IGISOL and JYFLTRAP Penning trap at the University
 86KR2c  of Jyvaskyla accelerator facility. Measured E|g, I|g using the         
 86KR4c  Valencia-Surrey Total Absorption Spectrometer consisting of a          
 86KR5c  cylindrical 12-fold segmented BaF{-2} detector, and |b|g-coin with a   
 86KR6c  0.5-mm-thick Si detector. Deduced |b feeding distributions using TAGS  
 86KR7c  analysis, and using a branching ratio matrix method so as to reproduce 
 86KR8c  |g-ray intensities profiles in high-resolution experiments.            
 86KR9c  Deduced accumulated Gamow-Teller transition strengths, and compared    
 86KRAc  with QRPA calculations.                                                
 86KR c  Previous studies of {+86}Br decay:                                     
 86KR c  1978LeZA (Table of Isotopes-1978): the decay scheme is adopted from a  
 86KR2c  private communication in 1977 from S. Prussin (University of           
 86KR3c  California, Berkeley). In comparison to earlier studies by 1975Hu02    
 86KR4c  and 1972Ac01, about 30 additional |g rays and six new levels were      
 86KR5c  reported in this communication, and the precision of E|g and I|g values
 86KR5c  was significantly better than that in previous studies. Consultation   
 86KR6c  by one of the evaluators (in February 2001) with S. Prussin suggested  
 86KR7c  that their work was not published, and a copy of the private           
 86KR8c  communication submitted to 1978LeZA was no longer available. A copy was
 86KR9c  not available from LBNL Isotopes Project.                              
 86KR c  1975Hu02: measured E|g, I|g, T{-1/2} of {+86}Br decay using Ge(Li)     
 86KR2c  detector. A total of 21 |g rays were reported from 498.0 to 6768.3 keV,
 86KR3c  but no decay scheme was proposed                                       
 86KR c  1972Ac01: measured E|g, I|g, T{-1/2}. Mass-separated source.           
 86KR2c  A total of 19 |g rays were reported from 499.8 to 6209.5 keV.          
 86KR3c  The decay scheme was proposed with nine excited states and 18 |g rays. 
 86KR c  1971Er15 (also 1970ErZZ): measured E|g, I|g, T{-1/2} of {+86}Br decay  
 86KR2c  Ge(Li) detector. A total of 19 |g rays from 533.2 to 5522 keV assigned 
 86KR3c  to {+86}Br decay. Another 17 |g rays from 94.4 to 4367 keV assigned to 
 86KR4c  {+86}Br or {+87}Br, but no decay scheme was proposed.                  
 86KR c  Others:                                                                
 86KR c  2018Fi03, 2017Fi06, 2014Fi09: Modular Total Absorption Spectrometer    
 86KR2c  (MTAS) system of 19 hexagonal shaped NaI(Tl) scintillators at          
 86KR3c  HRIBF-ORNL facility used to obtain beta feedings and average energy of 
 86KR4c  emitted |g radiation as 4110 keV in contrast to 3260 keV from the decay
 86KR5c  scheme from discrete |g-ray spectroscopy. Authors introduced 65 pseudo 
 86KR6c  levels to fit the observed total absorption spectrum, but the detailed 
 86KR7c  results of this study, in terms of individual level bins, and          
 86KR8c  respective |b feedings are not available.                              
 86KR c  1988Le21: measured E|g, I|g, yields                                    
 86KR c  1979Al05 (also 1982Al01): |b and |b|g coin                             
 86KR c  1977Ki14: T{-1/2} of {+76}Br decay                                     
 86KR c  1975Al11 (also 1973Jo02): total |g absorption spectra                  
 86KR c  1972Nu03, 1972Hi13: T{-1/2} of {+76}Br decay                           
 86KR c  1972KrYX: decay properties and yields                                  
 86KR c  1970Lu06: measured E|g, I|g, T{-1/2} of {+86}Br decay. Six |g rays     
 86KR2c  reported from 1365 to 6211 keV. An additional 4.5-s activity was       
 86KR2c  assigned to {+86}Br based on the initial growth of 1564|g. This        
 86KR3c  activity has not been confirmed in any of the later studies,           
 86KR4c  including that of 2016Ur04                                             
 86KR c  1966Wi03: |g, |g|g-coin, |b, |b|g-coin using NaI(Tl) detector.         
 86KR2c  15 |g rays reported from 1.21 to 6.7 MeV. Decay scheme was             
 86KR3c  proposed with seven excited states and ten |g rays.                    
 86KR c  1962St13: identified {+86}Br nuclide from {+86}Kr(n,p),E|?13 MeV,      
 86KR2c  followed by chemical separation. Measured |b and |g radiations using   
 86KR3c  scintillation counters, T{-1/2} of {+86}Br decay at Argonne National   
 86KR4c  Laboratory.                                                            
 86KR c  Theoretical calculations for |b decay of {+86}Br:

 97NB cL           The level scheme is based on E|g, I|g, |g|g data of 1968Si02 
 97NB2cL and modified and refined by subsequent measurements of E|g, I|g, |g|g, 
 97NB3cL by 1970Ar11, 1970Ho01, 1970Me06, 1970Mi02, 1972TiZS, 1975Co26. The     
 97NB4cL level scheme shown here omits the levels previously suggested at 1547  
 97NB5cL and 2056 keV. It is felt that the experimental basis for the placement 
 97NB6cL of the 804.52|g deexciting a level at 1547 keV is lacking; if this |g  
 97NB7cL deexcites a 1547-keV level, then the coin spectra of 1970Me06 require  
 97NB8cL that the 218.90|g is a triplet (feeding both the 1547 and 1548-keV     
 97NB9cL levels and also 1433-keV level). The 2056-keV level is omitted         
 97NBAcL because although the coin data (1970Me06) indicate that the 508|g is   
 97NBBcL a doublet, it has not been shown that it feeds the 1548 level          
 97NBCcL directly.                                                              
 97NB cL           Although seemingly well established, the decay scheme still  
 97NB2cL presents several difficulties: 1) |b{+-} feeding of the 1851.71 keV    
 97NB3cL {I5}/2+ level. 1970Me06 measure the E|b{+-}(max.)=825 {I30} keV in     
 97NB4cL coin with the 1851|g, implying direct |b{+-} feeding to this level,    
 97NB5cL yet strong 1851.61|g to g.s. will not allow J<5/2 or J|p=5/2- for this 
 97NB6cL level. The |b-group is, therefore, a second forbidden nonunique        
 97NB7cL transition which should have log| {Ift}>11.0, {Ii.e.}                  
 97NB8cL I|b{+-}<10|*10{+-3}%. 2) |b{+-} feeding of the 1750.43 keV {I5}/2+

 99TC DG RI        -------------------------------------------------            
 99TC DG RI        Calculating decay-scheme normalization factor.               
 99TC DG RI        I(g+e)(142g)=0.183 (11)X[1+40.2(6)] = 7.5 (5)                
 99TC DG RI        I(g+e)(140g)=744(11)X[1+0.1181(21)] = 832 (12)               
 99TC DG RI        T1/2(99Mo)/[T1/2(99Mo) - T12/(99mTc)] = 1.1                  
 99TC DG RI        SUMOF (g+e)(GS) = 56.9 (8)                                   
 99TC DG RI        At transient equilibrium:                                    
 99TC DG RI        [I(g+e)(142g)/1.1+I(g+e)(140g)/1.1+SUMOF (g+e)(GS)]XN=100%   
 99TC DG RI        That is:                                                     
 99TC DG RI        [7.5(5)/1.1+832(12)/1.1+56.9 (8)]XN = 820 (11) X N = 100%    
 99TC DG RI        So the normalization factor is                               
 99TC DG RI        N = 100 / 820 (11) = 0.1220 (16)                             
 99TC DG RI        The absolute intensity of the 140-keV gamma ray is given by: 
 99TC DG RI        g(140) = 744 (11) X N                                        
 99TC DG RI        To avoid including twice the uncertainty of                  
 99TC2DG RI        the 140-keV gamma ray:                                       
 99TC DG RI$g(140)=744(11)X100/[7.5(5)/1.1+744(11)X1.1181(21)/1.1+56.9(8)]=     
 99TC DG RI$=100/[7.5(5)/(744(11)X1.1) + 1.1181(21)/1.1 + 56.9(8)/744(11)]=     
 99TC DG RI$=100/[0.0092(6)+1.016(2)+ 0.0765(15)]= 100/1.1017(26)=90.8 (2)%     
 99TC DG RI$The absolute intensity of the 140-keV gama ray is:                  
 99TC DG RI        g(140) = 90.8 (2)%                                           
 99TC DG RI$Notice that if we had not included the cancellation effect the      
 99TC DG RI        (incorrect) result would have been:

100ZR c  2002Lh01: {+100}Y source was produced by 25-MeV p-induced fission of   
100ZR2c  {+238}U. Fission products were separated by the IGISOL separator. |g   
100ZR3c  rays were detected with four Ge detectors. Measured E|g, I|g,          
100ZR4c  |g|g-coin. Deduced levels, J, |p, |b-decay branching ratios, log {Ift}.
100ZR5c  Comparisons with theoretical calculations.                             
100ZR c  Others:                                                                
100ZR c  1977Kh03: {+100}Y source was produced from {+235}(U,F) with the JOSEF  
100ZR2c  gas-filled separator. |g rays were detected with Ge(Li) detector, x    
100ZR3c  rays were detected with a Ge detector and conversion electrons were    
100ZR4c  detected with a Si(Li) detector. Measured E|g, I|g, |g|g-coin,         
100ZR5c  |g(t),ce(t). Deduced levels, J, |p, |b-decay branching ratios,         
100ZR6c  log {Ift}, parent T{-1/2}.                                             
100ZR c  1977Pf01: measured E|g, I|g, T{-1/2}({+100}Y isotope) with the isotope 
100ZR2c  separator Lohengrin.                                                   
100ZR c  1979Bo26: measured selected E|g using curved-crystal measurement       
100ZR c  The identification of this isomer is based on the observation of       
100ZR2c  an intense 352|g, decaying with T{-1/2}=0.96 s and in coincidence      
100ZR3c  with the 212|g to the g.s. The 352|g is most likely the same as the    
100ZR4c  (4+) to 2+ transition observed in {+252}Cf SF decay. 1977Kh03 assigned 
100ZR5c  five |g rays to this isomer only, on the basis of T{-1/2} data, but the
100ZR6c  later work of 1986Wo01 showed that all these |g rays were also present 
100ZR7c  in the decay of the 735-ms isomer, with the difference that the 352|g  
100ZR8c  was much more intense in the spectrum obtained by 1977Kh03 and a       
100ZR9c  weak 1097|g was not reported by 1986Wo01. The source collection        
100ZRAc  procedures were different in 1977Kh03 and 1986Wo01, although both used 
100ZRBc  mass separation of fragments from neutron fission of {+235}U.          
100ZRCc  The recoil-separator method used by 1977Kh03 collected all the         
100ZRDc  activities of A=100 whereas only the {+100}Rb and {+100}Sr isotopes    
100ZREc  were collected in the method used by 1986Wo01. In the former, all      
100ZRFc  isomers of {+100}Y (high and low spin) would be observed whereas in    
100ZRGc  the latter mainly the low spin isomer would be detected since the      
100ZRHc  formation of {+100}Y was entirely due to {+100}Sr |b{+-} decay (g.s.   
100ZRIc  J|p=0+). It may also be pointed out that the |g-ray spectra shown by   
100ZRJc  1977Kh03 contain a much larger number of contaminants than those in    
100ZRKc  the spectra shown by 1986Wo01.                                         
100ZR c  Existence of isomerism in {+100}Y is confirmed in precision mass       
100ZR2c  measurements of 2007Ha32.

100ZR2c  code is in agreement with expected value of 9195 keV {I20}. However    
100ZR3c  the decay scheme is considered as incomplete in view of unrealistic    
100ZR4c  large |b feeding (thus low log| {Ift} values) to several |DJ=2,        
100ZR5c  |D|p=no levels in {+100}Zr probably due to unobserved transitions from 
100ZR6c  higher-energy levels. There is a large gap of about 7 MeV between      
100ZR7c  Q(|b{+-}) value and the highest known populated level at 2349

100NB c  2007Ri01 (also 2007RiZZ): isotopically separated 30-keV beam of        
100NB2c  {+100}Zr produced in U(p,F) reaction at E(p)=30 MeV using ion-guide    
100NB3c  isotope separator on-line (IGISOL) facility at JYFL. The fission       
100NB4c  fragments were accelerated to 30 keV and mass separated by a 55|'      
100NB5c  dipole magnet. The separated beam was injected into a gas-filled radio 
100NB6c  frequency quadrupole cooler and buncher (RFQ). Measured E|g, I|g,      
100NB7c  |g|g-, |b|g- and x|g-coin, fluorescent production using a planar       
100NB8c  plastic scintillator for |b particles, a large Ge detector and a planar
100NB9c  low-energy Ge detector for x rays and low-energy |g rays. Atomic mass  
100NBAc  measurements of {+100}Zr and {+100}Nb were made with a Penning-trap    
100NBBc  method using JYFLTRAP. Deduced levels, J, |p, conversion coefficient,  
100NBCc  |g-ray multipolarity, |b-decay branching ratios, log {Ift}. The photon 
100NBDc  intensities and uncertainties on gamma-ray energies and intensities    
100NBEc  were supplied as e-mail reply to B. Singh by S. Rinta-Antila on January
100NBFc  30, 2007 (2007RiZZ)                                                    
100NB c  2019Gu20: {+100}Zr isotope from U(p,F),E=25 MeV at the                 
100NB2c  IGISOL facility and JYFLTRAP double Penning trap system at the         
100NB3c  university of Jyvaskyla. Measured E|g, I|g, E|b, |b|g-coin, total      
100NB4c  absorption |g spectrum (TAGS) using Decay Total Absorption |g-ray      
100NB5c  Spectrometer (DTAS) with 18 NaI(Tl) crystals, a plastic |b detector    
100NB6c  and an HPGe detector.

147PM c  The {+147}Nd isotope was identified by 1946Bo25 in                     
147PM2c  {+146}Nd(n,|g),E=thermal reaction, with measurement of its half-life as
147PM3c  11.1 d {I2}, in agreement with the recommended value of 11.03 d {I3}.  
147PM4c  Earlier, 1941La01 (also 1942Ku03) had identified a 10-d activity in    
147PM5c  neodymium formed by bombarding Pr, Nd and Sm metals by |a particles,   
147PM6c  10-MeV deuterons, neutrons and |g rays. From current half-life values  
147PM7c  for Nd isotopes, this activity could only belong to {+147}Nd. Firm     
147PM8c  confirmation for the isotopic assignment of 11-d activity to {+147}Nd  
147PM9c  was made by 1947Ma28.                                                  
147PM c  {+147}Nd source was prepared using {+146}Nd(n,|g),E=thermal reaction   
147PM2c  in almost all the studies.                                             
147PM c  Note: this decay is important in fission yield determinations, reactor 
147PM2c  applications and in monitoring activity from long-lived fission        
147PM3c  fragments, such as by the CTBTO group. In particular, precise and      
147PM4c  accurate emission probability of the 531-keV gamma ray is needed for   
147PM5c  such applications. To address this requirement, recent experiments to  
147PM6c  measure absolute intensities (per 100 decays of {+147}Nd) have been    
147PM7c  carried out at three laboratories:                                     
147PM8c  LNHB-CEA, Saclay; LLNL + Texas A&M + ANL collaboration; and NPL, UK.   
147PM9c  However, final results are available only from LNHB-CEA, Saclay work in
147PMAc  2020Ke08, which are included in the present evaluation. Preliminary    
147PMBc  results are available from LLNL in 2020KoZZ report, which are also     
147PMCc  listed here in comments. In October 2021, evaluator                    
147PMDc  also received preliminary results from NPL, UK experiment through a    
147PMEc  private communication, but these results are not listed here. We hope  
147PMFc  to revisit the evaluation of this decay when final results from        
147PMGc  2020KoZZ, and from NPL, UK become available in open literature         
147PM c  Previous ENSDF/Nuclear Data Sheets evaluations: 2009Ni02, 1992De38,    
147PMxc  1978Ha22, 1967Ew01                                                     
147PM c  2013BeZP: DDEP evaluation of {+147}Nd decay, with a literature         
147PM2c  coverage up to March 2011. The evaluation presented in this dataset    
147PM3c  differs in many ways from the DDEP evaluation.                         
147PM c  Main references for E|g, I|g, |g(|q) and |g|g(|q) data:                
147PM c  2020Ke08: {+147}Nd source produced in {+146}Nd(n,|g) at the SmallBeBe  
147PM2c  facility in Delft, followed by separation and purification procedure   
147PM3c  using High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) coupled with an    
147PM4c  Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometer (ICPMS) at CEA-Saclay.    
147PM5c  Absolute activity of the source was measured at CEA-Saclay by two      
147PM6c  methods: 1. 4|p|b-coin using liquid scintillator for |b and NaI(Tl)    
147PM7c  detector for |g radiation; 2. 4|p|g counting using a well-type NaI(Tl) 
147PM8c  detector. High-resolution |g spectra were measured for two sets of six 
147PM9c  sources each one (series 1) using activity before purification and the 
147PMAc  other (series 2) after purification using a 100 cm{+3} HPGe detector,  
147PMBc  calibrated in efficiency to 0.4% above 100 keV and 1-2% below 100 keV. 
147PMCc  Weighted averages of the two sets of absolute photon intensities were  
147PMDc  reported for K{-|a2}, K{-|a1}, K{-|b1} and K|b{-2} x-rays, and 22 |g   
147PMEc  rays from 91 to 686 keV, including two extremely weak |g rays of 357.7 
147PMFc  and 366.5 keV, and with no evidence for the existence of 80.82, 117.9, 
147PMGc  159.7, 240.5 and 649.0 |g rays reported in 1997Sa53. The 80.82|g was   
147PMHc  interpreted as an escape peak of the strong 91.1|g. Absolute           
147PMIc  intensities of K{-|a} and K{-|b} x-rays were also measured. Results    
147PMJc  from this work have been included in the present evaluation.           
147PM c  2020KoZZ: LLNL, Texas A&M and ANL collaboration. Mass-separated        
147PM2c  {+147}Nd ion beam produced in fission by the CARIBU facility at ANL was
147PM3c  implanted on a thin carbon foil. Measured |b, ce, |g, |b|b-coin using  
147PM4c  a 4|p gas proportional counter for |b and ce (developed at LLNL), an   
147PM5c  HPGe detector with a superior efficiency response determination to     
147PM6c  0.5% in E|g=50-2000 keV region at Texas A&M. GEANT4 simulations were   
147PM7c  carried out for the detector systems. From |b|g-coin, total |b         
147PM8c  activity, and efficiency curves for |g and |b detection, absolute      
147PM9c  photon intensities were determined for 12 strong |g rays from 91.1 to  
147PMAc  695.9 keV, with 0.4% precision for the 531|g and 1.4% for the 91.1|g.  
147PMBc  Earlier results were also reported in Ph.D. thesis by A.M. Hennessy    
147PMCc  (University of California, Irvine, 2018). Results from this work have  
147PMDc  been quoted in comments, as these are still at a preliminary stage.

149ND5c  The {+149}Pr source was obtained from decay chain starting from        
149ND6c  {+149}Cs and {+149}Ba ({+149}Cs --> {+149}Ba --> {+149}La --> {+149}Ce 
149ND7c  --> {+149}Pr). The {+149}Cs and {+149}Ba were produced in {+235}U(n,F),
149ND8c  E=thermal at OSIRIS on-line fission-product mass separator facility in 
149ND9c  Studsvik. The A=149 activities were mass separated and deposited on a  
149NDAc  mylar tape. Measured |b|g|g using NE111A plastic scintillator, one low-
149NDBc  energy x-ray detector and a 50% HPGe detector. Lifetime measurements   
149NDCc  were made by |b|g|g(t) using fast timing coincidence between NE111A |b 
149NDDc  detector and BaF{-2} |g detector together with coin requirement with   
149NDEc  a |g ray detected in a Ge detector.

154SM cB $The I|b{+-} to the excited levels have been deduced independently of  
154SM2cB the |g data from the total absorption |g spectrometer, TAGS, data of   
154SM3cB 1997Gr09. The measured spectrum represents approximately the |b{+-}    
154SM4cB feeding intensity as a function of the excitation energy. When         
154SM5cB necessary, new levels, called "pseudolevels", and associated decay |g's
154SM6cB are included in the analysis.  Since the resolution of the TAGS system 
154SM7cB is typically 50-100~keV, the intensity assigned to a pseudolevel may   
154SM8cB represent the |b{+-} feeding to a single level or to a group of levels 
154SM9cB in that region.                                                        
154SM cB IB        Values are from |g intensity balances, except those for      
154SM2cB      the 0- and 82-keV levels which are from measurements of 1995Gr19. 
154SM3cB      The quoted uncertainties do not include any contribution from     
154SM4cB      the possible placement of the unplaced |g's.                      
154SM5cB      The I|b{+-} values from the TAGS data (1997Gr09) are generally    
154SM6cB      in excellent agreement with those from the intensity balances.    
154SM7cB      The TAGS value is given in a comment if it differs by more        
154SM8cB      than 10%. Since the decay scheme is not complete, values          
154SM9cB      below 0.2% are not given.

156SM c  1990He11: {+156}Sm, from thermal-neutron fission of {+235}U followed by
156SM2c  isotope separation. Source material collected on a movable tape and    
156SM3c  transported to a counting station. Measured multiscaled |g singles     
156SM4c  using a large-volume coaxial Ge detector and a LEPS detector.  Measured
156SM5c  simultaneously low-energy |g's and ce's using the LEPS and an          
156SM6c  ion-implanted Si detector. System geometry was calibrated using |g's of
156SM7c  known multipolarities from the {+124}In decay. Measured |g|g and

156SM9c  detectors. Report E|g, I|g, Q(|b{+-}), T{-1/2} values for two excited  
156SMac  states. The ce data are not reported in 1990He11, but some of the      
156SMbc  deduced multipolarities are given there.

156SM cB           The I|b{+-} values have all been computed from the           
156SM2cB  |g-transition intensity balances and therefore are accurate only      
156SM3cB  insofar as this decay scheme is correct and complete. There are 3     
156SM4cB  unplaced |g rays with intensities of |?0.6% and, since the weakest    
156SM5cB  reported |g's have intensities of 0.3%, it is reasonable to expect    
156SM6cB  that there are unobserved |g rays with intensites of 0.2% and less.   
156SM7cB  With a Q value of 5150 keV and the high spin (J=4) of the parent,     
156SM8cB  it is expected that many levels above that at 2699 keV will be        
156SM9cB  populated, albeit weakly. Therefore, a minimum uncertainty of 0.4%    
156SM0cB  has been assigned to each I|b{+-} by the evaluator.                   
156SM cB $1995Gr19, using total-absorption |g spectroscopy, deduce that the |b  
156SM2cB branching to the ground and first excited states is 1.8% {I17}. These  
156SM3cB authors point out that their data do not provide evidence for a nonzero
156SM4cB |b- branch to the first excited state.                                 
156SM cB           The I|b{+-} to the 803 and 1009 levels have been set to zero 
156SM2cB  because the adopted J|p requires that these transitions be negligibly 
156SM3cB  weak. The values deduced from the intensity balance are 2.0% {I3} and 
156SM4cB  2.1% {I8}, respectively.
